newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African wool prices higher at latest auction.
newsitem.headline: S.African wool prices higher at latest auction.

text.p: South African wool prices were higher at the latest weekly auction, the Wool Board said.
It said 11,476 bales were offered at this week's sale, of which 96.8 percent was sold.

Price quotes for long Merino fleeces of 20 micron rose 5.0 percent, 21 micron rose 4.0 percent, 22 micron rose 0.3 percent, 23 micron rose 0.1 percent, 24 micron fell 1.0 percent and 25 micron fell 0.8 percent.
Prices for Merino bellies fell 1.9 percent, Merino lambs rose 4.2 percent and Merino locks fell 0.3 percent.
The offering included 1,882 bales of other White Wools, 1,197 bales of Ciskei/Transkei, 2,173 bales of Lesotho and 1,178 bales of coarse and coloured.

Of the 405 bales of 20 micron offered, 96.8 percent was sold. Of the 1,239 bales of 21 micron offered, 97.4 percent was sold. Of the 2,147 bales of 22 micron offered, 98.4 percent was sold. Of the 1,799 bales of 23 micron offered, 98.3 percent was sold. Of the 845 bales of 24 micron offered, 99.3 percent was sold and of the 281 bales of 25 micron offered, 98.2 percent was sold.
The next sale will take place on June 11, when about 10,000 bales will be on offer.
